title: 9-round AES-256: reported whole-key related-key basic filter

target.description: The authors' reported whole-key attack on 9-round AES-256, with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The detailed filter stage is separately recorded as aes256-9r-integral-fklssww2001-related-key-basic; its selected subkey material and the broader whole-cipher claim have different scopes.

setting.key_relation: For an unknown base master key L, L_a XOR L has byte a at zero-based master-key byte indices 21 and 25 and zero elsewhere, for every a in 0,...,255. The a=0 key is the base key; total distinct keys is 256.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Eight varying plaintext bytes cover 2^64 choices under each of 256 related master keys, totaling 2^72 key/plaintext queries.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.
Related master keys use a fixed XOR relation, while their expanded-key differences depend on guessed base-key bytes through S-boxes. These are not arbitrary independently selectable subkey oracles.

This record retains the paper's explicit whole-cipher attack headline. The detailed search first isolates selected subkey material; repeated filtering, reverse expansion or residual search for full master-key completion is not separately costed for every endpoint in this version.

time.note: Section 4.2 estimates 2^248 guesses and a workload comparable to one encryption per guess. This basic endpoint has different data and key guessing from the partial-sum improvement. This whole-key row preserves the authors' attack-level estimate; it does not infer a new constant factor from the separately catalogued filter.

data.note: Total across 256 distinct related keys: 2^64 chosen plaintexts per key. The factor 256 is already included. The acquisition budget is the paper's reported attack-level budget.

memory.note: Neither the basic nor improved related-key construction provides an explicit complete peak-storage budget.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: No numerical success for this exact key_recovery output is given. Section4.2 says enough sets identify the correct guesses; Section4.3 says about32 structures, without a joint error probability. The source 256-key relation and required plaintext compensation are conditions of the balanced identity. The basic 2^72-data endpoint does not inherit the optimized structure count or an invented per-set rejection rate. This is an author full-key headline; numerical success of unitemized completion is not inferred from the selected-subkey relation.
